sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A lost workspace's memory and permissions both came back
sections.para: Mondweep Chakravorty's 104.7-second video replays a twelve-step run: Ruflo stores two facts, an ABP-governed adapter saves an encrypted SGit checkpoint, the project is deleted, and a fresh process restores it with the same SHA-256. Three safeguards hold. Recall by meaning was not validated; the MIT code has 16 tests.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Both facts restored exactly, and three safeguards held
sections.para: After the original was deleted, both facts came back exactly in a fresh process, with a matching SHA-256, and out-of-scope access was refused, unapproved deletion stopped and a tampered copy rejected. Recall by meaning was switched off and marked not validated. Ruflo and SGit are pinned, with 16 tests and evidence in the repository.

sections.label: The question
sections.line: A real run tests whether agent memory survives loss
sections.para: If a container is recycled or a project deleted, does an agent's memory return with its rules? Mondweep Chakravorty's 104.7-second video, published 17 October 2026, answers with a real run. His MIT code, mondweep/sgit-ruv-memory, has a four-tool MCP server, an ABP-to-Ruflo compiler, 16 tests and run evidence.

sections.label: The run, in twelve steps
sections.line: Twelve steps: pin, store, refuse, save, delete, restore, verify
sections.para: Ruflo v3.56.10 and a pinned SGit commit run four ABP rows. Two Kestrel facts are stored; a forbidden namespace is refused; an encrypted checkpoint binds data to policy; unapproved deletion stops; the project is deleted. A fresh process restores matching SHA-256, Ruflo reads both facts, a missing key stays missing, and tampering fails closed.

sections.label: What it proves, and what it says it does not
sections.line: A real loss-and-restore loop, honest about its scope
sections.para: Both facts were recovered and unauthorised access, unapproved deletion and an altered checkpoint were blocked; recall by meaning, real-world value and reliability remain to validate. The repository's runner also matched keyword search after restore, with semantic recall partial. Unlike most demos it deletes for real, restores in a new process and tests refusals.

sections.label: Why it matters to me
sections.line: Vault memory and behaviour policy, together on camera
sections.para: It is the first time someone outside our own sessions has combined an encrypted vault as agent memory with a behaviour policy beside the prompt, inside someone else's agent stack, on camera. It is the hive, memory and mandate that Agentics, ready to sell describes, and Mondweep is named there to deliver it.

sections.label: Where to go next
sections.line: Open questions: when the vault is used, and bypasses
sections.para: The architecture piece explains why the vault is written or read in only three of twelve steps, on one machine, inside the adapter. The third piece asks what it means that Ruflo's own command line reaches the memory file without the policy. Readers can also step through the run.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A proof of concept, analysed from screen and code
sections.para: The audio was not transcribed and the code was read, not run, by this site. It is a proof of concept, with reliability and real-world value still to validate. Only exact recall was tested, the Kestrel facts are synthetic, and the analysis is Claude's, checked against the frames by this site's agent.
